Fast Retailing reported its fifth consecutive year of record profit on Thursday, as Uniqlo sales rose across every region and new store openings in the United States and Europe drove growth beyond its traditional Japanese and Chinese markets.

# Fast Retailing FY2026 annual earnings: record profit for 5th year
Fast Retailing reported its fifth consecutive year of record profit on Thursday, as Uniqlo sales rose across every region and new store openings in the United States and Europe drove growth beyond its traditional Japanese and Chinese markets.

Net profit for the fiscal year ended August 31 rose 25% to 542.52 billion yen. Annual revenue grew 17% to 3.9633 trillion yen, and business profit climbed 30% to 718.4 billion yen, the company said.

The results beat analyst expectations. A consensus of analysts polled by data provider Visible Alpha had projected net profit of 510.7 billion yen, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Fast Retailing's international Uniqlo operations were the standout performer, with revenue rising 26% to 2.4111 trillion yen and business profit expanding 44% to 439.8 billion yen.

North America posted a 35% revenue gain to 364.9 billion yen and a 53% jump in business profit, while Europe's revenue rose 39% to 512.6 billion yen and its business profit expanded 69% to 91.7 billion yen.

North America contributed 9.2% of total company revenue during the fiscal year, with Europe at 13%.

In Greater China, where profit fell the previous year amid weak consumer demand, business profit rose 25% to 112.0 billion yen.
